title: Review Tracks, Acknowledgment and Decision Clocks, and Case Records in Appeals and Grievances
content:
## Appeals and Grievances review tracks, time limits and case documents

**Clause.** A case is acknowledged within the tier's acknowledgment period in business days of receipt, and decided within the tier's decision time limit counted in the tier's unit from receipt; business days are Monday through Friday excluding federal holidays. Acknowledgment moves the case from filed to under review, assigned to a reviewer, and the acknowledgment letter carries the case reference.

**Expedited track.** A case meets the expedited track only under the tier's expedited criteria (an ongoing inpatient stay or a delay that could seriously jeopardize life or health), as certified by the treating provider; the beneficiary's own urgency alone does not move a case. A standard case that meets the criteria is moved to the expedited track where the tier allows standard-to-expedited movement, and an expedited request that does not meet them continues on the standard track where the tier allows expedited-to-standard movement.

**Records.** The reviewer may ask for records; the appellant has the tier's records window to send them, after which the case is decided on the record. Every document the tier lists as required must be on file before a decision.

**Open-case condition for documents.** Records requests and documents are recorded only on a case whose status is filed or under review.

### Judgement points

| Case status | Records request or document recorded? |
|---|---|
| filed | yes |
| under review | yes |
| any other status (decided, dismissed, withdrawn, escalated) | no |

| Treating provider's certification of the expedited criteria | Beneficiary's own urgency | Meets the expedited track |
|---|---|---|
| present | any | yes |
| absent | stated | no |

**Counting business days (hypothetical).** A case received on a Thursday, with a 5-business-day acknowledgment period and no federal holiday in the week that follows: Friday is business day 1, the following Monday to Thursday are days 2 to 5, so acknowledgment falls no later than the following Thursday. A federal holiday on that Monday pushes the fifth business day to the Friday.
